trust_decision.summary: Whether a user-supplied post-login 'next' URL is on-site is decided in one shared helper, get_next_path, which only clears scheme/netloc via urlsplit and so passes forms the browser reads as off-site (///host, /\host, leading control chars, javascript:/data:/file: schemes).

landing_point.why: Summary says 'post-login redirect handling'; the password login handler redirect(next_path) at redash/handlers/authentication.py:187-199 leads straight to get_next_path, the only function with an open-redirect comment.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET/POST /login and /<org_slug>/login (redash/handlers/authentication.py:176-199); also /ldap/login, /remote_user/login and /oauth/google_callback through the same helper

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix only changes the shared helper. Google OAuth saves the raw 'next' in the session (redash/authentication/google_oauth.py:95) and checks it again on reload (redash/authentication/google_oauth.py:139-142), so the helper fix covers it automatically. It is not a separate fix site.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who patches the password-login handler inline rather than the helper could argue Google OAuth is a separate SSO feature whose next value comes from the server-side session, not from the request, so it is trusted. The argument is weak because the session value is copied unchecked from request.args at redash/authentication/google_oauth.py:49,95.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Relative next paths ('queries') must pass through unchanged, and same-site absolute or protocol-relative URLs with a path ('//localhost/queries', 'https://myredash.com/queries/5') must be cut down to their path rather than rejected. If 'next' is missing, the index URL is the default. An over-broad fix that rejects anything with a netloc, or anything without a leading '/', breaks the existing tests.

O6_input_shapes: http(s) or protocol-relative URL with netloc (path extracted)

O7_producer.where: Google OAuth's session['next_url'] (redash/authentication/google_oauth.py:95) is the only state that crosses a boundary, and the check runs on it when it is read back (redash/authentication/google_oauth.py:142)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The SAML ACS callback honours the RelayState form field as the post-login redirect without calling get_next_path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SP-initiated SAML usually carries the return URL in RelayState. login.html already passes next= to the SAML login link (redash/templates/login.html:24), but at the pinned commit sp_initiated drops it, so a maintainer finishing that feature would plausibly redirect(request.form['RelayState']) directly.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: org_login validates 'next' with a separate local check (e.g. startswith('/')) before storing it, instead of relying on the callback's get_next_path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Org-scoped OAuth entry is a separate route that already handles next itself. A local 'is relative' check would be a second, weaker implementation that a solver might fix or not, depending on whether the callback still validates.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The verify-email page takes next_url from request.args for its meta-refresh (redash/templates/verify.html:4) instead of url_for('redash.index').
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Post-verification 'return to where you were' is a common feature request, and the template already renders a next_url.

O9_family: CWE-601 open redirect (URL parser differential between Python urlsplit and browsers)

O10_build.toolchain: uv (pyproject.toml, per recent commit f41b859d), pytest
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_authentication.py class TestRedirectToUrlAfterLoggingIn (tests/test_authentication.py:258-295) posts to /login?next=... and asserts response.location

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject next values that start with '//' (or require a leading single '/'), missing backslash, control-char and scheme forms, or breaking the existing relative 'queries' and '//localhost/queries' behaviour.

out_of_scope_notes: redash/authentication/saml_auth.py:109-146 uses allow_unsolicited=True (line 60) for SAML responses; this is unrelated to the redirect property and was not pursued.
